ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A thin concavo-convex lens made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$ has a convex surface with a radius of curvature of $20 cm$ and a concave surface with a radius of curvature of $60 cm$. The convex side of the lens is silvered, creating a concave mirror, and is placed on a horizontal surface.

1. (a) Where should a pin be placed on the optical axis such that its image is formed at the same place?
2. (b) If the concave part is filled with water of refractive index $\frac{4}{3}$, find the distance through which the pin should be moved so that the image of the pin again coincides with the pin.

(b) If the concave part is filled with water of refractive index $\frac{4}{3}$, find the distance through which the pin should be moved so that the image again coincides with the pin.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A thin concavo-convex lens made of glass with refractive index $1.5$ has a convex surface of radius of curvature $20\,\text{cm}$ and a concave surface of radius of curvature $60\,\text{cm}$. The convex side of the lens is silvered, forming a concave mirror. (a) Where should a pin be placed on the optical axis so that its image is formed at the same place? (b) If the concave part is filled with water of refractive index $\frac{4}{3}$, find the distance through which the pin should be moved so that the image again coincides with the pin.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: No separate image evidence is needed here; I use the geometry stated in the problem and the assigned reading: the pin is on the concave/non-silvered side, and the convex surface of radius 20 cm is silvered so it acts as a concave mirror for the light inside the lens. (a) For the glass meniscus lens in air, take converging power as positive. The convex surface has radius 20 cm and the concave surface has radius 60 cm, so the ordinary thin-lens power is P_g=(1.5-1)(1/20-1/60)=0.5(3-1)/60=1/60 cm^-1. The silvered convex surface acts as a concave spherical mirror of radius 20 cm, so its focal length is 10 cm and its mirror power is P_m=1/10 cm^-1. For a silvered thin lens, the ray passes through the lens twice, so P_eq=2P_g+P_m=2(1/60)+1/10=1/30+1/10=2/15 cm^-1. Thus the equivalent focal length is f_eq=1/P_eq=15/2=7.5 cm. For the image to coincide with the object in an equivalent concave mirror system, the object must be at the equivalent centre of curvature, i.e. at 2f_eq: 2f_eq=15 cm. So the pin should initially be placed 15 cm in front of the lens on the concave side. (b) When the concave hollow is filled with water of refractive index 4/3, the water-filled concavity contributes the power of a thin water lens of radius 60 cm. Its power is P_w=(4/3-1)(1/60)=1/180 cm^-1. This water lens is also traversed twice, so the new equivalent power is P'_eq=2P_g+2P_w+P_m =2(1/60)+2(1/180)+1/10 =1/30+1/90+1/10 =(3+1+9)/90=13/90 cm^-1. Hence f'_eq=90/13 cm, and the new equivalent centre of curvature is 2f'_eq=180/13=13.85 cm approximately. The pin was originally at 15 cm, so the required displacement is 15-180/13=15/13=1.15 cm approximately, i.e. 1.16 cm. Since the new coincident position is smaller than 15 cm, the pin must be moved toward the lens.
